text:
kevin: heads up — multiple customers reporting 502/504s to the hosted inference endpoint since ~09:12 UTC. spike on edge-proxy metrics (5xx up ~12x). sample req id: `req-0a1f2b3c`. reproducible with this curl:

```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' \n  -H 'X-Request-ID: req-0a1f2b3c' \n  -d '{"model":"gpt-lite","input":"short prompt"}'
```

response: `HTTP/2 502` with empty body. customers also see long tail 504s for streaming requests. tagging @sara for support triage. :boom:

infra-bot: deploy-notice: `edge-proxy/nginx` config v2026.03.17-09:05 rolled at 09:07:14 UTC to 100% of traffic (change: upstream keepalive tuning + tls renegotiate opt). See: https://ci.redwood.local/edge-proxy/rolls/2123

sara: on it. can you paste the upstream hostnames / route or sample trace (envoy ids)? also: which customer is hitting this most? any correlating auth errors in the same window?

kevin: top impacted customers: acme-inc, betaapps, and a couple of small PLG users. envoy trace header on failed req: `x-envoy-upstream-service-time: 0` and upstream log shows `upstream connection reset before headers`. we see auth service returning `200` but with much higher latency (200-800ms) during the spike. pattern: streaming + larger payloads first, then smaller sync requests.

maria: quick checks — 1) confirm upstream conn pool saturation + resets, 2) check tls session reuse stats, 3) see if the new tls renegotiate opt caused connection churn. can you grab `nginx.error.log` around 09:06-09:20 for host `edge-ww-1` and `edge-ww-2`? also pull `envoy.cluster.upstream_rq_5xx` metric by cluster.

josh: if auth latency is elevated it can cause head-of-line blocking on pooled connections. temporary mitigation: increase upstream pool size or disable the tls renegotiate flag on the nginx canary. we can also flip a route rule to send streaming-heavy tenants to the dedicated cluster while we investigate.

kevin: uploading selected logs (excerpt):

```
[09:08:12] nginx[edge-ww-1]: 2026/03/17 09:08:12 [error] 2345#0: *992 upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream, client: 10.2.5.23, server: api.redwood.ai, request: "POST /v1/generate HTTP/2.0", upstream: "https://upstream-auth-1:443/", host: "api.redwood.ai", ref: "req-0a1f2b3c"
[09:09:03] envoy[edge-ww-1]: cluster_upstream_rq_5xx{cluster="upstream-auth"} 128
```

kevin: reproduced locally by hammering streaming endpoint with 8 concurrent streams, saw ~20% 502s after ~60s. repro steps: run script below from lab env against canary endpoint:

```
# repro script (bash)
for i in {1..8}; do
  ./stream-test.sh --concurrency 1 --duration 90 &
done
wait
```

sara: good repro, thanks. next actions: (1) disable the nginx tls renegotiate flag on canary (rollback config) — maria/josh can you coordinate? (2) open short-term route diversion for streaming tenants -> dedicated cluster (jackson-csm please notify customers), (3) collect full nginx+envoy traces and auth svc spans for 09:00-09:30 window. i'll own the support comms. :white_check_mark:

maria: i pulled the canary and started config rollback at 09:18 UTC. deploying rollback to 100% now. monitoring metrics.

jackson-csm: pinging impacted CSMs and sending holding note to ACME and BetaApps: explaining we saw edge proxy instability, we've rolled back a recent change and are monitoring. will follow up with root cause.

infra-bot: deploy-notice: `edge-proxy/nginx` config v2026.03.17-09:05 rolled back at 09:20:10 UTC (roll id 2123 -> rollback 2123-r1).

kevin: spike subsided after rollback (~09:21). 5xxs back to baseline. opening a postmortem ticket and attaching traces. i'll add the repro script and a short checklist so support can respond faster if it recurs.

josh: follow-ups for postmortem: verify connection reuse semantics between nginx and auth svc, add load tests for streaming patterns during config rollouts, add circuit-breaker to fallback to dedicated pool when upstream latency >200ms for 30s.

sara: thanks all — i'll close the incident once postmortem is filed and customers are updated. :handshake:
